t: Palindrome Partitioning IV - Precomputed Palindrome Table Plus a Three-Way Split
o: Decide whether a string of up to 2000 lowercase letters can be cut into three non-empty pieces, each of which is a palindrome: `abcbdd` = `a` + `bcb` + `dd` succeeds, while `bcbddxy` admits no such split. Any candidate partition is pinned down by two cut points 0 < i <= j < n - piece one is s[0..i-1], piece two s[i..j], piece three s[j+1..n-1] - so there are only O(n^2) splits to try. The trap is re-verifying palindrome-ness from scratch inside the split loop, which degrades to roughly 10^10 operations at n = 2000. Precomputing once, for every substring, whether it is a palindrome costs O(n^2) time and space and turns each three-piece verification into two array lookups.
k: Every three-way partition is determined by two cut indices; enumerate pairs of cuts, never individual characters.
The palindrome table satisfies pal[i][j] = (s[i] == s[j]) and (length <= 2 or pal[i+1][j-1]); filling rows right-to-left guarantees the interior is ready when needed.
Prune aggressively: if the prefix s[0..i-1] is not a palindrome, the entire first-cut row can be skipped.

a.i: Enumerate the cut points and verify each of the three pieces with an inward-walking two-pointer scan. Early exits - first mismatch inside a piece, skipping whole rows whose prefix piece already failed - make it behave well on typical inputs and need zero extra memory. The worst case remains cubic, however, which can time out at n = 2000.
s: Write helper is_pal(i, j) that shrinks two pointers inward.
Loop the first cut i from 1 to n-2; skip immediately if s[0..i-1] fails.
Loop the second cut j from i to n-2; return true if all three pieces pass.
Return false after both loops finish.
a.t: O(n^3) worst case - O(n^2) split pairs, each potentially triggering O(n) scans; pruning improves constants, not asymptotics.

a.n: Approach 2: DP Palindrome Table with O(1) Split Checks
a.i: Precompute pal[i][j] for every substring using the classic recurrence: the endpoints must match, and either the substring has length 1 or 2 or the interior pal[i+1][j-1] must already be a palindrome - hence iterate i downward. The split enumeration then performs nothing but table lookups, giving genuine O(n^2) overall with early termination on the first valid triple.
s: Fill the table: for i from n-1 down to 0, for j from i to n-1, set pal[i][j] by the recurrence.
For each first cut i from 1 to n-2, skip unless pal[0][i-1].
For each second cut j from i to n-2, return true iff pal[i][j] and pal[j+1][n-1].
Return false if no split qualifies.
a.t: O(n^2) - quadratic table construction plus a quadratic scan whose inner work is O(1).

w: Always build the table; treat the brute force as a conversation starter only. If asked to optimize further, mention the bitset refinement - each row of the palindrome table can be maintained as shifted/masked machine words, accelerating construction by the word size (~64x), worthwhile when n reaches tens of thousands. Pitfalls: off-by-one on the middle piece (it spans i..j with j <= n-2 so the final piece stays non-empty); reading uninitialized interiors by filling the table top-down instead of bottom-up; and forgetting all three pieces must be non-empty, i.e., 1 <= i <= j <= n-2. Follow-ups: minimum number of palindromic pieces (the Partitioning II family), counting all valid triples, or allowing up to k character changes.
